   "source": [
    "# MCMC sampling and priors\n",
    "\n",
    "This notebook covers the MCMC tools in `psiphy.mcmc` and the prior specifications in\n",
    "`psiphy.utils.prior`:\n",
    "\n",
    "1. Priors: uniform, log-uniform, Gaussian and mixtures\n",
    "2. Sampling a posterior with `MHSampler` (emcee backend)\n",
    "3. Convergence diagnostics: traces, autocorrelation time, burn-in\n",
    "4. Checking the result against the analytic posterior\n",
    "5. Saving, reloading and extending a chain\n",
    "6. Informative priors\n",
    "\n",
    "The test problem is `NoisyLine` (a straight line with Gaussian noise). Its posterior is\n",
    "Gaussian with a closed form, so every result can be checked exactly.\n",
    "\n",
    "Related notebooks: *Nested sampling and evidence* (posterior + Bayes factors),\n",
    "*Importance sampling and SMC*, *Likelihood-free inference* (simulator only)."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "251a2b95",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-14T14:13:56.872159Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-14T14:13:56.871893Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-14T14:13:58.595266Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-14T14:13:58.594829Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import os\n",
    "import tempfile\n",
    "\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "\n",
    "from psiphy.mcmc import MHSampler\n",
    "from psiphy.utils.prior import UniformPrior, LogUniformPrior, GaussianPrior, MixturePrior\n",
    "from psiphy.toy_models import NoisyLine\n",
    "from psiphy.plotting.diagnostics import SampledDistribution, plot_triangle\n",
    "\n",
    "np.random.seed(42)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "a4550e70",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "---\n",
    "## 1  Priors\n",
    "\n",
    "Every prior in `psiphy.utils.prior` shares one interface, so the same object works with\n",
    "MCMC, nested sampling, importance sampling/SMC and BOLFI:\n",
    "\n",
    "| Method | Purpose |\n",
    "|---|---|\n",
    "| `sample(n)` | draws, shape `(n, ndim)` |\n",
    "| `log_prob(theta)` | single point → float; batch `(n, ndim)` → `(n,)` |\n",
    "| `prior_transform(u)` | unit cube → parameters (used by nested sampling) |\n",
    "| `to_scipy()`, `to_torch()`, `to_sbi()` | conversion to other libraries |"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "6f224779",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-14T14:13:58.596887Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-14T14:13:58.596732Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-14T14:13:58.864978Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-14T14:13:58.864413Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 1500x300 with 4 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "priors = {\n",
    "    'Uniform(0, 10)':              UniformPrior([(0, 10)]),\n",
    "    'LogUniform(0.1, 10)':         LogUniformPrior([(0.1, 10)]),\n",
    "    'Gaussian(5, 1.5²)':           GaussianPrior([5.0], [1.5**2]),\n",
    "    'Mixture: 0.3 N(2,.5²) + 0.7 N(7,1²)': MixturePrior(\n",
    "        [GaussianPrior([2.0], [0.25]), GaussianPrior([7.0], [1.0])], weights=[0.3, 0.7]),\n",
    "}\n",
    "\n",
    "grid = np.linspace(0.01, 11, 500)[:, None]\n",
    "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(15, 3), sharey=False)\n",
    "for ax, (name, p) in zip(axes, priors.items()):\n",
    "    ax.hist(p.sample(20000)[:, 0], bins=60, range=(0, 11), density=True, alpha=0.5, label='samples')\n",
    "    ax.plot(grid[:, 0], np.exp(p.log_prob(grid)), 'k', lw=1.5, label='exp(log_prob)')\n",
    "    ax.set(title=name, xlabel=r'$\\theta$')\n",
    "axes[0].legend(fontsize=8)\n",
    "plt.tight_layout()\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "4cabba03",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Named bounds can be passed as a dict; the keys become `prior.names` and are picked up by\n",
    "the samplers. `prior_transform` maps uniform draws on $[0,1]^d$ to the prior, which is how\n",
    "nested samplers use it."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "id": "38aa8958",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-14T14:13:58.866370Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-14T14:13:58.866281Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-14T14:13:58.868874Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-14T14:13:58.868305Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "names            : ['slope', 'intercept']\n",
      "log_prob (inside): -4.094344562222101\n",
      "log_prob (batch) : [-4.09434456        -inf]\n",
      "prior_transform  : [0. 5.]\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "prior = UniformPrior({'slope': (-3, 3), 'intercept': (0, 10)})\n",
    "print('names            :', prior.names)\n",
    "print('log_prob (inside):', prior.log_prob([0.0, 5.0]))\n",
    "print('log_prob (batch) :', prior.log_prob(np.array([[0.0, 5.0], [9.0, 5.0]])))\n",
    "print('prior_transform  :', prior.prior_transform([0.5, 0.5]))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "f3fea2c8",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "---\n",
    "## 2  Problem: fitting a noisy line\n",
    "\n",
    "Data: $y_i = m x_i + b + \\varepsilon_i$ with $\\varepsilon_i \\sim \\mathcal{N}(0, \\sigma^2)$\n",
    "and known $\\sigma$. With a flat prior the posterior on $(m, b)$ is Gaussian with\n",
    "covariance $\\sigma^2 (A^\\top A)^{-1}$, where $A = [x, 1]$, centred on the least-squares fit."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "id": "52356705",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-14T14:13:58.870051Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-14T14:13:58.869973Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-14T14:13:58.904324Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-14T14:13:58.903523Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "analytic posterior mean: [-0.816  5.188]\n",
      "analytic posterior std : [0.043 0.248]\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 600x350 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "line = NoisyLine(Nx=40, noise_sigma=0.8)\n",
    "theta_true = np.array([-0.8, 5.0])\n",
    "y_obs = line.simulate(theta_true)\n",
    "\n",
    "def log_posterior(theta):\n",
    "    lp = prior.log_prob(theta)\n",
    "    return lp + line.log_prob(theta, y_obs) if np.isfinite(lp) else -np.inf\n",
    "\n",
    "# analytic posterior (flat prior, posterior well inside the box)\n",
    "A = np.column_stack([line.x, np.ones_like(line.x)])\n",
    "post_cov = line.noise_sigma**2 * np.linalg.inv(A.T @ A)\n",
    "post_mean = np.linalg.solve(A.T @ A, A.T @ y_obs)\n",
    "print('analytic posterior mean:', post_mean.round(3))\n",
    "print('analytic posterior std :', np.sqrt(np.diag(post_cov)).round(3))\n",
    "\n",
    "plt.figure(figsize=(6, 3.5))\n",
    "plt.plot(line.x, y_obs, '.', label='data')\n",
    "plt.plot(line.x, theta_true[0] * line.x + theta_true[1], 'r-', label='truth')\n",
    "plt.xlabel('x'); plt.ylabel('y'); plt.legend()\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "55404a99",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "---\n",
    "## 3  Running `MHSampler`\n",
    "\n",
    "`MHSampler` wraps `emcee.EnsembleSampler`. Starting from a single point, the walkers are\n",
    "spread into a small Gaussian ball (`init_scale`, relative). Starting from prior draws,\n",
    "pass an array of shape `(n_walkers, n_dim)`."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "83192da0",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-14T14:13:58.906433Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-14T14:13:58.906258Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-14T14:13:59.924109Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-14T14:13:59.923640Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "chain shape (steps, walkers, dim): (3000, 32, 2)\n",
      "mean acceptance fraction        : 0.712\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "sampler = MHSampler(log_posterior, n_walkers=32, param_names=prior.names)\n",
    "sampler.run(prior.sample(32), n_steps=3000, progress=False)\n",
    "\n",
    "print('chain shape (steps, walkers, dim):', sampler.get_chain().shape)\n",
    "print('mean acceptance fraction        :', sampler.acceptance_fraction.mean().round(3))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e61f60eb",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "---\n",
    "## 4  Convergence diagnostics\n",
    "\n",
    "Walkers start spread over the whole prior and need some steps to reach the posterior.\n",
    "The integrated autocorrelation time $\\tau$ measures how many steps it takes for the\n",
    "chain to forget its state. Common practice: discard a few $\\tau$ as burn-in and run for\n",
    "at least ~50 $\\tau$. `discard=\"auto\"` drops $3\\,\\max(\\tau)$ steps."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 6,
   "id": "b66bb3da",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-14T14:13:59.925330Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-14T14:13:59.925258Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-14T14:14:00.063744Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-14T14:14:00.063023Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "autocorrelation time: [25.7 31.6]  → auto burn-in = 94 steps\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 1000x500 with 2 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "chain = sampler.get_chain()\n",
    "tau = sampler.autocorr_time()\n",
    "burn = int(3 * tau.max())\n",
    "print('autocorrelation time:', tau.round(1), ' → auto burn-in =', burn, 'steps')\n",
    "\n",
    "fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(10, 5), sharex=True)\n",
    "for i, (ax, name) in enumerate(zip(axes, prior.names)):\n",
    "    ax.plot(chain[:, :, i], 'k', alpha=0.1, lw=0.6)\n",
    "    ax.axhline(theta_true[i], c='r', lw=1)\n",
    "    ax.axvline(burn, c='C0', ls='--', label='auto burn-in')\n",
    "    ax.set_ylabel(name)\n",
    "axes[0].legend(loc='upper right')\n",
    "axes[-1].set_xlabel('step')\n",
    "plt.tight_layout()\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "63adfd73",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [

   "source": [
    "samples = sampler.get_chain(flat=True, discard='auto', thin=5)\n",
    "print('MCMC mean :', samples.mean(0).round(3), '   analytic:', post_mean.round(3))\n",
    "print('MCMC std  :', samples.std(0).round(3), '   analytic:', np.sqrt(np.diag(post_cov)).round(3))\n",
    "\n",
    "fig = plot_triangle(samples, labels=['m', 'b'], true_values=theta_true, engine='corner',\n",
    "                    bins=40, plot_datapoints=False, fill_contours=True, levels=(0.68, 0.95))\n",
    "# overlay the analytic 1σ/2σ ellipse in the 2-D panel\n",
    "ax = fig.axes[2]\n",
    "vals, vecs = np.linalg.eigh(post_cov)\n",
    "t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 200)\n",
    "for k in (1, 2):\n",
    "    ell = post_mean[:, None] + vecs @ (k * np.sqrt(vals)[:, None] * np.vstack([np.cos(t), np.sin(t)]))\n",
    "    ax.plot(*ell, 'C1--', lw=1)\n",
    "fig.suptitle('MHSampler vs analytic posterior (orange dashed: 1σ, 2σ)', y=1.02)\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "cf840230",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "**Why is $b$ not centred on the truth?** The MCMC result matches the analytic\n",
    "posterior, and that posterior is centred on the least-squares fit to *these* 40 points.\n",
    "The noise in this particular data set moves that fit away from the true line by a fraction\n",
    "of a standard deviation (printed below). Every correct method follows the data; checking\n",
    "for *bias* requires many data sets — see Section 7 of the *Importance sampling and SMC*\n",
    "tutorial."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 9,
   "id": "7a1ddcd2",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-14T14:14:00.186883Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-14T14:14:00.186804Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-14T14:14:00.188974Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-14T14:14:00.188439Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "least-squares fit: [-0.816  5.188]  truth: [-0.8  5. ]  offset (sigma): [-0.38  0.76]\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "offset = (post_mean - theta_true) / np.sqrt(np.diag(post_cov))\n",
    "print('least-squares fit:', post_mean.round(3), ' truth:', theta_true, ' offset (sigma):', offset.round(2))"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "---\n",
    "## 6  Saving, reloading and extending a chain\n",
    "\n",
    "Pass `filename=` to store the chain in HDF5 (needs `h5py`). The file can be reloaded, and\n",
    "`run(n_steps=...)` without a starting point continues from the last state — useful for\n",
    "long jobs on a cluster with wall-time limits."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 11,
   "id": "462d3704",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-14T14:14:00.196077Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-14T14:14:00.196017Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-14T14:14:02.074407Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-14T14:14:02.073996Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "first job : 500 steps\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "after resume: 1500 steps stored in line_chain.h5\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()\n",
    "fn = os.path.join(tmpdir, 'line_chain.h5')\n",
    "\n",
    "s1 = MHSampler(log_posterior, n_walkers=32, filename=fn)\n",
    "s1.run(prior.sample(32), n_steps=500)\n",
    "print('first job :', s1.n_steps, 'steps')\n",
    "\n",
    "# later, e.g. in a new job:\n",
    "s2 = MHSampler.load(fn, log_prob_fn=log_posterior)\n",
    "s2.run(n_steps=1000)\n",
    "print('after resume:', s2.n_steps, 'steps stored in', os.path.basename(fn))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "fa055d99",

   "source": [
    "---\n",
    "## 7  Informative priors\n",
    "\n",
    "Swapping the prior is a one-line change. A Gaussian prior on the intercept (say from an\n",
    "earlier measurement) tightens the intercept and, through the correlation, the slope."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 12,
   "id": "45ec1125",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-14T14:14:02.075563Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-14T14:14:02.075490Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-14T14:14:03.907566Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-14T14:14:03.906835Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 1000x350 with 2 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    },
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "std flat       : [0.043 0.247]\n",
      "std informative: [0.029 0.128]\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "prior_inf = GaussianPrior(mean=[0.0, 5.0], cov=[10.0**2, 0.15**2], names=['slope', 'intercept'])\n",
    "log_post_inf = lambda t: prior_inf.log_prob(t) + line.log_prob(t, y_obs)\n",
    "\n",
    "s_inf = MHSampler(log_post_inf, n_walkers=32).run(prior.sample(32), n_steps=3000)\n",
    "samples_inf = s_inf.get_chain(flat=True, discard='auto', thin=5)\n",
    "\n",
    "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3.5))\n",
    "for i, (ax, name) in enumerate(zip(axes, prior.names)):\n",
    "    ax.hist(samples[:, i], bins=50, density=True, alpha=0.5, label='flat prior')\n",
    "    ax.hist(samples_inf[:, i], bins=50, density=True, alpha=0.5, label='Gaussian prior on b')\n",
    "    ax.axvline(theta_true[i], c='r')\n",
    "    ax.set_xlabel(name)\n",
    "axes[0].legend()\n",
    "plt.tight_layout()\n",
    "plt.show()\n",
    "print('std flat       :', samples.std(0).round(3))\n",
    "print('std informative:', samples_inf.std(0).round(3))"
